entities.name: House of Habsburg-Lorraine
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The House of Habsburg-Lorraine, created when Holy Roman Empress Maria Theresa's husband Francis I of Lorraine merged his Lorraine dynasty with the Habsburg house upon their 1736 marriage, represents the continuation of Habsburg imperial rule from 1740 (Maria Theresa's succession) through Austria-Hungary's 1918 dissolution — the most recent form of the dynasty. Though Maria Theresa technically ruled as 'Queen of Hungary and Bohemia' (Salic law barred her from Holy Roman Emperor), she was Austria's most consequential ruler: she reformed administration, education, and the military while waging the War of Austrian Succession (1740-1748) against Frederick the Great.

Maria Theresa (r. 1740-1780) — mother of 16 children including Marie Antoinette (who became Queen of France and was executed in the Revolution) — introduced compulsory primary education to her lands, founded the Vienna General Hospital, abolished the use of judicial torture, and reformed the tax system. Her son Joseph II (r. 1780-1790) continued her reforms, abolishing serfdom (1781) and granting religious toleration (Edict of Toleration, 1781) — he was the 'most enlightened despot' in European history.

The dynasty continued through Napoleon's defeat (1815), the Hungarian Compromise (1867 creating Austria-Hungary), Franz Joseph's 68-year reign (1848-1916), and Franz Ferdinand's assassination (1914) that triggered WWI. Charles I (r. 1916-1918), the last Habsburg emperor, abdicated November 11, 1918 — the same day WWI ended — dissolving the multinational empire that had governed 50+ million people across 11 nations. He was beatified by Pope John Paul II in 2004.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The House of Habsburg-Lorraine — producing Maria Theresa's Enlightenment reforms, governing 50 million people across 11 nations in Austria-Hungary, and ending in WWI's catastrophe — governed Central Europe's most diverse empire and its dissolution created the modern map of Central Europe.
